newsitem.title: FRANCE: Freight little hit by French air strike.
newsitem.headline: Freight little hit by French air strike.

text.p: A strike by pilots at British
Airways -controlled French airlines, Air Liberte and TAT European Airlines, has had little impact on freight activity, company sources told Reuters.
The strike, which began on April 9, is over the terms and conditions of a merger between Air Liberte and TAT, which took effect April 1.

"While our domestic flight network is only operating to around 40 percent of normal levels, we have managed to maintain our long and mid-haul services which are the most important for freight," an Air Liberte cargo official said.
Air Liberte operates daily passenger services from Paris to the French West indies and three weekly frequencies to Reunion, in the Indian Ocean, using DC10-30 aircraft.
The carrier's mid-haul network from Paris includes Casablanca, Marrakech and Agadir using MD83s.
Meanwhile, a TAT cargo spokesman told Reuters, the strike was having "a very limited effect" on the airline's freight activities.

"Services we operate on behalf of BA, for example, Paris-London, Bordeaux-London and Toulouse- London have been maintained while two of our main domestic routes from Paris to Toulon and Perpignan, are operating normally too." - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
